findings.title: Verified, namespaced tools
findings.requirement: Identify each tool by a verified server identity plus the tool name. Base server identity on the verified endpoint, credential, or registry namespace. A server's self-reported name is neither unique nor trustworthy. Flag lookalike and duplicate names across servers. Test that a new server can't quietly swap its tool in for an approved one.

A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved

findings.title: Enforced gateway boundary
findings.requirement: Send MCP calls through a gateway or equivalent enforcement layer the agent cannot bypass. Choose controls for internal HTTP servers, public third-party services, and local stdio servers; private networking and mTLS are one internal deployment pattern, not universal MCP requirements. Authenticate each caller, preserve agent and delegated-subject identity, and authorize each action's tool, operation, resource, tenant, and arguments. Apply the same policy to direct calls, dynamic tools, CLI/code mode, and wrappers. Validate calls and responses, enforce rate limits, and log every decision. For HTTP OAuth, validate access tokens for the gateway's own audience, issuer, expiry, and scopes; obtain separately authorized backend credentials through a trusted issuer or supported exchange. Never accept a token for another resource or relay it unchanged as a substitute for backend authorization. Keep backend secrets and tokens away from agent-controlled execution paths. Restrict local process launch, files, environment, credentials, and network in the host or sandbox. Under MCP 2026-07-28, reject metadata-header/body mismatches before routing or policy relies on them. Isolate private caches by verified authorization context, tenant, resource, and policy version; share only data explicitly approved as public. Authorize explicit task/state handles on every operation; neither a connection nor self-reported metadata establishes identity. Where the gateway is an OAuth client, validate authorization-server issuer responses and protect discovery URLs against SSRF. Record protocol and extension versions and test each enabled extension's boundary, including task access/cancellation and MCP Apps sandbox, CSP, bridge messages, and UI-initiated tool authorization. Test bypass, cross-tenant access, malformed traffic, and required-check outages. Required checks fail closed.

not_covered.problem: Tool inventory missing a task-based reason for each tool
Agent credential granting wildcard or admin permissions
Destructive actions running without a higher-authority approval
Hidden instructions inside a tool's metadata
Outbound traffic to unapproved internet destinations

evidence.note: Exchanged tokens are cached by (audience, scope, tenant) only. The same token is shared by parent and child instances.

findings.title: Untrusted peer messages
findings.requirement: Authenticate the sending agent (prove its identity) on every message, even validly signed ones. Validate message types and schemas, and check what that peer is allowed to ask for. Where a replay could repeat an action, check freshness and track nonces or request IDs. Checking the sender alone doesn't stop replays. Test faked identity, replayed requests, requests across tenants, and instructions passed along by a compromised peer. Verify signed agent cards where they exist. A card says who an agent is, not what it may do. Check callback and webhook URLs against SSRF. A valid sender doesn't make a message's content trusted.

findings.title: Bounded delegated authority
findings.requirement: Give sub-agents only the powers approved for their task. Preserve the verified original subject and current actor through each handoff and enforce their task, tenant, resource, and audience limits where the action runs. Use supported token exchange or narrow task credentials rather than copying a parent's full credential. A parent must not gain a denied power by asking a more powerful peer to act without separate valid approval. For RFC 8693 tokens, earlier nested actors are provenance only and never add access. An actor chain or signed identity does not prove that a requested action was approved. Test legitimate delegation and that escalation attempt.

not_covered.problem: Approvals that can be replayed or aren't tied to exact arguments
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded
Children still running after the parent is stopped
Replayed or faked peer-agent messages
No limit on how many sub-agents a run can start

evidence.note: The child runs as role 'line_item_extractor' (extractor.py:25) but tools.yaml defines only 'extractor', so the lookup falls back to the full 'procurement' tool set, including pay_invoice, create_purchase_order, erp_call and extract_line_items. The child also uses the same TokenBroker and workload token as the parent, and token_for keys on audience, scope and tenant only (identity.py:95), so no task-narrowed child credential exists.

findings.title: Recursive shutdown
findings.requirement: Run a drill across a parent, nested children, remote workers, queued work, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks, where they exist. Check that the stop reaches every descendant within the set time. It must revoke access as needed and prevent orphaned retries or restarts. Record how outside effects that already happened are reconciled.

not_covered.problem: Agent able to disable or delay its own stop
No way to cut off the agent's access without cutting off the user
No drill for a compromised shared tool or agent type
Sub-agent given powers beyond its task

evidence.note: The halt flag is read once, at run start. The model loop (loop.py:139), tool dispatch (loop.py:53) and the extractor child loop (extractor.py:64) never re-read it, and runs are untracked asyncio tasks (main.py:159), so a halt reaches no in-flight run, child or open call. A halted tenant's running agent and its children continue.

checks.check: A stop signal from the root reaches every descendant: nested children, remote workers, queued work, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks.
checks.verify: 1) Find the stop handler. 2) Check it reaches nested children, remote workers, queued jobs, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks (cancel calls, MCP `notifications/cancelled`). 3) Answer no if any of these that exists in the code is not reached, or stop only sets an in-process flag that remote workers never read.
checks.note: The halt flag is read once, at run start. The model loop (loop.py:139), tool dispatch (loop.py:53) and the extractor child loop (extractor.py:64) never re-read it, and runs are untracked asyncio tasks (main.py:159), so a halt reaches no in-flight run, child or open call. A halted tenant's running agent and its children continue.

checks.check: Stopping revokes descendants' credentials or leases, and leases or tokens are short-lived, so a disconnected worker loses authority within the stop time limit.
checks.verify: 1) Open the stop path and credential issuing code. 2) Check stopping revokes descendants' tokens or leases. 3) Check token or lease lifetime fits within the stop time limit. 4) Answer no if no revocation exists, or tokens are long-lived so a disconnected worker keeps authority.
checks.note: No stop path revokes descendant tokens or leases. Cached exchanged tokens stay in use until expiry (lifetime set by the outside STS, unknown here), and the 600s workload token (deployment.yaml:107) is longer than any visible stop limit.

checks.check: Queues and schedulers refuse new work, retries, and restarts for a stopped tree.
checks.verify: 1) Find queue consumers, schedulers, and retry logic. 2) Check each looks up the stopped state before running new work, retries, or restarts. 3) Answer no if any consumer, retry decorator, or restart policy runs without that check.
checks.quote: async def extract(self, parent: RunIdentity, doc_id: str, budget: Budget) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
checks.note: Only run start checks the halt flag. Spawning a sub-agent (extractor.py:42-44) and every later step skip the stopped-state lookup, so a halted tree can still start children and do new work. No stopped-tree state is kept.

checks.check: Outside effects already completed are recorded for reconciliation.
checks.verify: 1) Open the stop path. 2) Check it records outside effects already completed (tool calls, writes, sent messages) for reconciliation. 3) Answer no if nothing is recorded, or only in-flight work is listed.
checks.note: The halt path only raises; it records no completed effects. Per-call tool_result audit rows with operation_id exist (loop.py:95), which could support reconciliation, but no stop-time record or reconciliation procedure is in this repo (the runbook is referenced as external).

red_flags_found: app/killswitch.py:25 assert_running is called only at run start (loop.py:127); halts do not stop running agents or sub-agents
violates: Check that the stop reaches every descendant within the set time
findings.summary: The kill switch is checked only when a run starts, so a halt does not stop running agents, their children or their open calls, and nothing revokes their tokens.
findings.next_step: Check the halt flag every model turn and tool call in the parent and child loops, track and cancel run tasks, revoke or shorten leases on stop, and record completed effects for reconciliation.
